---
title: Range requests return bytes in an encoding the client accepts
description: Uncached range requests now forward the client's Accept-Encoding header, and cached encoded ranges go only to clients that accept the encoding.
products:
  - cache
date: 2026-11-23
---

Range requests now return bytes in an encoding the client accepts. The change covers ranges served from cache and ranges fetched from your origin without caching.

## Cached encoded files

A range of a cached file encoded with gzip or Brotli counts bytes of the encoded file. Cloudflare now serves that range only if the client accepts the encoding. Otherwise, Cloudflare ignores `Range` and sends the complete, decompressed file as `200 OK`. Cloudflare always sends the complete file for a cached file encoded with Zstandard or `deflate`.

Previously, a client that did not accept the encoding could receive a `206 Partial Content` response whose bytes did not match its `Content-Range` header.

## Uncached range requests

If caching is bypassed or the request is not eligible for caching, Cloudflare forwards the client's `Range` header to your origin. On HTTPS, Cloudflare now also forwards the client's own `Accept-Encoding` header. Previously, Cloudflare sent its default header, which lists `br` and `gzip`. Cloudflare passes your origin's `206 Partial Content` response to the client without decoding it, so a client could receive a range in an encoding it did not accept.

If a client sends no `Accept-Encoding` header, your origin can receive an empty one. Your origin should answer an empty `Accept-Encoding` header with an unencoded response.

Range requests that Cloudflare serves from cache, or fetches with Origin Range Requests, still send Cloudflare's own `Accept-Encoding` header to your origin.

For more information, refer to [Range request behavior](/cache/reference/range-requests/).
